accessibility.title: Friction module introduction static overview
accessibility.long_description: A text-first overview of Friction. Model dry-friction contacts and determine static, impending, or kinetic regimes across sliding, tipping, wedges, screws, belts, collars, bearings, and rolling resistance.

objective: Model dry-friction contacts and determine static, impending, or kinetic regimes across sliding, tipping, wedges, screws, belts, collars, bearings, and rolling resistance.
prerequisites: Use contact free-body diagrams, normal-force direction, equilibrium, impending-motion sense, moments, and consistent force and angle units.

worked_example.entry_description: Adjust normal force, static and kinetic coefficients, and required tangential force; classify the regime and reveal the actual friction force without assuming static friction is always at its maximum.

diagram_description: The planned contact and friction-regime workspace will support: adjust normal force; adjust static friction coefficient; adjust kinetic friction coefficient; adjust required tangential force; classify static impending or kinetic regime; show actual and limiting friction vectors; toggle contact free-body diagram; compare tipping and sliding thresholds; adjust wedge screw belt bearing and rolling-resistance parameters. Until v1.1.0 is published, this description and procedure map are the complete accessible fallback.
